findings.title: [P1] Parse the cached value rather than the metadata wrapper
findings.body: On every cache hit, `loadProfile` fails. `Cache.get` now returns `{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null`, but `src/profile.ts:20` still calls `JSON.parse(cached)` on the wrapper object. TypeScript rejects the argument (`{ value: string; stale: boolean }` is not assignable to `string`); if type checking is bypassed, `JSON.parse` coerces the object to `"[object Object]"` and throws a `SyntaxError`. The line should read `JSON.parse(cached.value)`. The surrounding `cached === null` miss-handling is otherwise correct.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported Cache.get return contract
findings.body: `Cache.get` is exported and previously returned `string | null`; it now returns a metadata object, a breaking signature change that directly contradicts the PR's stated intent of "preserving existing contracts." The only in-repo consumer is `loadProfile` (covered above), so no additional breakage is provable here, but any external consumer relying on the old contract would stop compiling or silently receive an object. If this contract change is intentional, document it as breaking; otherwise keep `get` returning `string | null` and expose metadata via a separate method.
